children: Mexico's finance ministry projects economic growth of up to 2.5% in 2027, down from the up to 2.8% expansion projected for 2026 in the budget document, according to the proposal published on Tuesday.
The budget deficit is forecast to narrow to 3.9% of gross domestic product (GDP), down from the 4.1% projected for 2026, Finance Minister Edgar Amador said.

The ministry also projected headline inflation to finish 2027 at 3.0%, aligning with the Bank of Mexico's updated guidance last month, which delayed its timeline for reaching the 3.0% inflation target to the fourth quarter of 2027.
The document laid out that state oil firm Pemex is slated to receive 81.1 billion pesos to pay down debt amortizations, compared to 263.5 billion pesos in the prior budget.
